A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching authors, core theory, and HetGPS algorithm. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–R support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations and learning results for matrix games, Multi-goal-capture, Tag, Football, and HetGPS, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds an unequal-size matrix game and an 8-chaser/3-escapee Tag experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the heterogeneity-gain objective, environment-gradient updates, and alternating/concurrent training procedures are unchanged. The additional experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds a many-agent/few-task matrix scenario in Table 10 and an 8-chaser/3-escapee Tag scenario in Appendix L. These extend agent-to-task balance and pursuit conditions within existing domains; the earlier task coverage remains.

E2.justification: Both versions compare neurally heterogeneous and homogeneous teams trained with MAPPO. No additional implemented comparison algorithm is evaluated; the selected reward-aggregator combinations are experimental conditions.

E3.justification: The added 8v3 Tag experiment uses 1000-step episodes, reduced parallel sampling, a reported 30M-frame budget, and five aggregator pairs. The added matrix experiment reports 12M frames. Existing protocols remain unchanged. New documentation contains inconsistencies: Appendix J.4 names 12 agents while Table 10 specifies 11, and Figure 9 labels 0–500 million frames despite its 30M-frame caption.

E4.justification: Appendices J.4 and L add focused checks of whether predicted gain patterns persist with unequal agent/task counts, larger teams, and longer horizons. The existing observability analysis, trajectory examples, and adverse-initialization test are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across random seeds. Existing run counts remain unchanged, and the added experiments follow the established practice with eight seeds. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or statistical test is introduced.

E6.justification: v4 adds matrix results in Table 10 and 8v3 Tag results in Figure 9 and Appendix L, including gains of 1.243 ± 0.615 for (min, mean) and -0.990 ± 1.025 for (mean, max). Tables 11–12 supply numerical endpoints for retained Figure 4 experiments. These are additional reported results, not same-setting performance improvements; the Football table changes only numerical precision.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 3.1–3.4, sum-form analysis, and appendix proofs and derivations are unchanged. The added explanation that constant-sum task scores are required specifically by Theorem 3.3 clarifies an existing assumption rather than revising it.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same principal contributions: characterizing heterogeneity through reward curvature, introducing HetGPS, and demonstrating empirical connections to MARL. The additional validation does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly warns that empirical stability does not guarantee HetGPS convergence and that oscillation is possible. Appendix R.4 expands applicability guidance concerning symmetry, monotonicity, constant-sum assumptions, and partially matching reward functions. Appendix M qualifies the Football generalization as requiring further verification, while Appendix L discusses learning limitations at larger scales.

D1.justification: Appendix B changes the stated code-delivery mechanism from an attached supplement to a link on the supplementary website. A new reproducibility statement identifies README instructions and training, HetGPS, and plotting code. The network architecture, hardware, and timing details in Appendix C are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section and cited-work membership are unchanged. Positioning relative to behavioral-diversity methods, task allocation, and environment co-design remains the same.

P1.justification: v4 locally rewrites the introductory aggregation explanation, edits terminology and wording, adds a reproducibility statement, and expands and retitles Appendix R. The overall section organization and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 10–12 and Figure 9, enlarges several main-text figures, and corrects two aggregator labels in Figure 4a. Tables 11–12 additionally display existing learning-curve endpoints. Later displays are relocated and renumbered, and conference headers are added without a wholesale layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 improves auditability through endpoint tables, corrected legend labels, and clearer scope and convergence caveats. However, the added validation contains unresolved contradictions: Table 10 claims exact theoretical agreement despite negative entries where Table 2 predicts zero, and Appendix L treats (mean, max) as a nonpositive control although Table 2 predicts positive gain. Figure 9 also conflicts with its reported frame budget. These inconsistencies make the reliability of the added evidence, and thus the net quality improvement, uncertain.
